correctness.rationale: In the polar Q the coordinate potential differences satisfy |xij|≤1 and each blade has pairwise differences ≤1. At vertices the tight-edge graph must be connected, forcing each blade to contain nonzero signed {0,1} potential values of only one sign; the converse active-edge spanning criterion supplies all (2^(q+1)−2)^m facet labels. After orthogonal mean subtraction the squared polar norm is k−s²/(mq+1). Any maximizing assignment with |s|>q can flip a concordant blade and decrease |s| without changing k, contradiction. For m≥3 adding a missing same-sign blade leaf raises squared norm by at least (m−2)q/(mq+1)>0; for m=2 the bound k−s²/N≤2q with balanced full leaves settles equality. Thus maximizers have k=mq and balanced signs, yielding the radius and exact binomial contacts. Central symmetry shows no offset ball can be larger. Antipodal contact inequalities force optimal centers perpendicular to all farthest polar vertices; the remaining finite inequalities have strict slack at zero, proving full relative interior in that complement. Contact sign vectors span rank m−1 (even) or m (odd), giving stated dimensions. Independently enumerated six (m,q) pairs using exact fractions, agreeing with max squared norms and contact counts; the unbounded proof comes from the sign-flip and rank arguments.
residual_risks: Correctness specific to ordinary ambient norm on zero-sum space, not deleting hub coordinate.
The asserted complete optimal-center set is characterized only by affine dimension/relative interior, not all inequalities or volume.
